name: Lockheed Martin
description: Lockheed Martin designs, builds and supports military aircraft, missiles and air defense, helicopters and naval combat systems, and space systems. One customer dominates: the US Government was 72 percent of 2025 sales (63 percent from the Department of War) and the rest is mostly foreign governments buying either through US Foreign Military Sales or directly. The F-35 fighter alone is 27 percent of sales. Work is done under long-term government contracts, either cost-reimbursable (the government pays costs plus a fee) or fixed-price, and revenue is booked as work is performed. Profit therefore depends on cost control on fixed-price programs: 2025 included large reach-forward losses (a $950M classified Aeronautics program, $570M on the Canadian Maritime Helicopter Program). Backlog was $193.6B at year-end 2025.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source. SEC SIC code is 3761 (Guided Missiles & Space Vehicles & Parts) per EDGAR. Mowgli classification is not set here.

hq.note: 6801 Rockledge Dr., Bethesda, MD 20817 (EDGAR business address); incorporated in Maryland

employees.note: Approximately 123,000 including about 72,000 engineers, scientists and IT professionals; about 93% in the US. FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: Aeronautics
businessLines.how: The US Government and allied governments (directly or through Foreign Military Sales) pay per aircraft delivered under production contracts, and pay annual fees for sustaining fleets (spare parts, maintenance, upgrades), so the F-35's installed base creates recurring sustainment revenue; profit is contract price minus cost, with fixed-price programs carrying the loss risk.
businessLines.description: Military aircraft: F-35 Lightning II (67% of segment sales in 2025), F-16, C-130 Hercules, F-22 sustainment, unmanned systems and advanced development programs.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $2,523M; FY2023 $2,825M. Includes a $950M reach-forward loss on a classified program (Q2 2025) and $140M unfavorable C-130 adjustments

businessLines.name: Missiles and Fire Control (MFC)
businessLines.how: The US Army, Navy and Air Force and allied governments pay per missile or launcher delivered under multi-year production contracts, plus support services; profit rises with production volume once a line is ramped. Sales grew 14% in 2025 from a JASSM/LRASM/PAC-3 ramp.
businessLines.description: Air and missile defense (PAC-3, THAAD), tactical and strike missiles (GMLRS/MLRS, PrSM, JASSM, LRASM, Hellfire, JAGM), fire control and sensors.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $413M (after $805M of net unfavorable profit adjustments incl. a classified-program loss); FY2023 $1,541M

businessLines.name: Rotary and Mission Systems (RMS)
businessLines.how: Governments pay per helicopter or system delivered plus fixed multi-year service and sustainment fees; profit depends on cost performance, and two international helicopter programs (Canada's CMHP, Turkey's TUHP) took reach-forward losses in 2025.
businessLines.description: Sikorsky helicopters (Black Hawk, Seahawk, CH-53K King Stallion, Combat Rescue Helicopter), naval combat systems (Aegis), radar, missile defense systems, command and control, cyber and training.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $1,921M; FY2023 $1,865M. 2025 includes $570M loss on CMHP and $95M on TUHP

businessLines.name: Space
businessLines.how: NASA, the Navy, the Missile Defense Agency and the Space Force pay under cost-reimbursable development and production contracts for satellites, launch-related systems and strategic missiles; long-lived programs (Trident, Orion) give steady multi-year revenue.
businessLines.description: Satellites, space transportation systems (Orion crew vehicle for NASA), strategic missiles (Trident II D5 for the Navy), Next Generation Interceptor for missile defense, advanced strike and hypersonics.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $1,226M; FY2023 $1,158M. 2025 includes $130M favorable adjustments on commercial civil space programs
